t: A cattle kingdom of south-western Uganda ruled by the Hinda dynasty, whose kingship was embodied in the royal drum Bagyendanwa.
Its society was divided between Bahima herders, who held power, and Bairu farmers, who formed the majority.
The 1901 Ankole Agreement enlarged it under British rule; it was abolished in 1967 and never restored.
dyk: In Nkore the kingship was embodied in the royal drum Bagyendanwa, which had its own shrine, attendants and herds, and a king's sons traditionally fought one another for the throne.
ev: Ruhinda traditionally founds the Hinda dynasty of Nkore
Ntare IV Kitabanyoro repels an invasion from Bunyoro
Ntare V becomes king and extends Nkore's influence over its neighbours
Rinderpest destroys most of the kingdom's cattle
Ntare V dies; Kahaya II is installed with Nuwa Mbaguta's support
The Ankole Agreement enlarges the kingdom within the Uganda Protectorate
Charles Gasyonga II succeeds Kahaya II
Uganda's new constitution abolishes the kingdom

f.capital: Shifting royal kraals; Mbarara from c. 1900
